oidc_jwt.description: A valid unexpired bearer access token can be reused across multiple API calls and sessions.
oidc_jwt.source: RFC 6750 behavior reflected by Casdoor OAuth usage docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same bearer token as replay unless the artifact is documented as one-time.

oidc_jwt.description: Acceptance of tokens without nbf, or lack of nbf enforcement, is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report missing nbf enforcement alone as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: On SSO logout, Casdoor invalidates tokens by setting ExpiresIn to 0 or a negative value; introspection and refresh reject tokens with ExpiresIn <= 0.
oidc_jwt.source: Token overview - Token lifecycle and invalidation
oidc_jwt.note: Post-logout token rejection is expected and should be used as the freshness oracle.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and documents them as interchangeable.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token and id_token payloads as token confusion by themselves.

oidc_jwt.description: Shared applications intentionally use organization-qualified client identifiers with the suffix -org-<organizationName>.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat org-suffixed client IDs as cross-tenant confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: When an admin changes application or provider trust configuration, acceptance under the new configuration is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: General platform configuration model and provider/application admin workflows
oidc_jwt.note: Only flag stale acceptance of old trust anchors after an intended rotation point, not success under the newly authorized configuration.

oidc_jwt.description: Old signing keys may remain accepted until cache expiry when JWKS-based trust is cached.
oidc_jwt.note: Only treat old-key acceptance after cache expiry as suspicious.

oidc_jwt.description: When an admin reconfigures providers, applications, issuer bindings, or trusted upstream settings, new logins following the updated configuration are expected.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance under the new admin-approved trust configuration as a trust-anchor substitution bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor issues access_token and id_token with the same JWT payload and treats them as interchangeable.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag identical access_token/id_token claims as over-issuance by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: Casdoor can automatically link external OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone, or case-insensitive username.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges under configured auto-linking are by design, not necessarily principal-binding failures.

oidc_jwt.description: For external SAML IdPs, if username mapping is absent or empty, Casdoor falls back to email and then NameID for username creation.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity values may differ from the original upstream field by design in SAML-backed accounts.

oidc_jwt.description: With exclusive sign-in enabled, a new login removes all previous sessions for that user and application.
oidc_jwt.note: Loss of older sessions after a new login is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 freshness tests against /api/login/oauth/access_token, always run a CONTROL login first with a valid token/code flow before sending expired or future-dated artifacts. Without a successful control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken client/application setup.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 docs; token issuance examples and grant flow requirements

oidc_jwt.constraint: Casdoor supports PKCE on the authorization code flow. If code_challenge/code_challenge_method=S256 were sent to /login/oauth/authorize, the token request to /api/login/oauth/access_token MUST include the original code_verifier. With PKCE enabled, client_secret is optional, but if provided it must be correct. Do not interpret token exchange failure without code_verifier as an identity-binding bug; it is expected PKCE enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 docs; Custom OAuth provider docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For RFC 8707 resource indicator tests, the resource parameter must match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI instead of the client_id when resource is used. A mismatch causes failure by design and must not be misclassified as audience-validation vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 docs - Binding Tokens to Specific Services

oidc_jwt.constraint: Use access_token as the session credential for subsequent API calls. Although Casdoor documents that access_token and id_token are the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably, session_token MUST still be mapped to access_token because /api/userinfo and other API calls are documented to use the access token.

Refresh token lifetime has a numeric sentinel: application Refresh Token expiration default is 0 hours. Value 0 does not mean immediate expiry; it selects the platform default configuration. Do not assume 0 disables refresh or means zero lifetime without confirming the application setting.

Code resend timeout has a numeric sentinel: application Code resend timeout value 0 means use the global default, not literal zero seconds. Do not treat 0 as 'no wait' in tests that depend on verification-code timing.
oidc_jwt.source: Application configuration docs - Verification Code Settings

oidc_jwt.constraint: CookieExpireInHours has a numeric sentinel: value 0 means use the default session cookie lifetime, not zero hours. The documented default is 720 hours, and without Remember me the session is limited to 24 hours. Do not use 0 expecting immediate expiry.

Casdoor's /api/sso-logout revokes the authenticated user's current session or all sessions depending on logoutAll. It is not an admin endpoint that accepts an explicit token value. Cleanup logic must call it with the target session's own bearer token; do not attempt admin-driven arbitrary token revocation via this endpoint.

For I5 token-exchange scope escalation tests, request a narrower original scope first, then exchange with a broader requested scope. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, and specified scope is intended to narrow permissions to a subset of the original token's scope. Treat issuance of broader claims than the original scope as the oracle condition.

For audience-binding tests on token exchange and resource indicators, inspect aud via /api/login/oauth/introspect because /api/userinfo returns claims according to scope and may not expose all token metadata needed for the oracle. Use introspection with Basic client authentication to confirm active, aud, iss, exp, and sub.
oidc_jwt.source: OAuth 2.0 docs - token introspection and userinfo

oidc_jwt.constraint: Casdoor applications are organization-scoped, and shared applications use an organization-qualified client identifier suffix '-org-<organizationName>'. For cross-org or cross-tenant audience tests, use the exact org-qualified client_id when targeting a shared application; otherwise failures may be due to wrong client binding rather than proper audience enforcement.

Applications and providers are attached to organizations, and only built-in can create shared applications. In multi-tenant tests, ensure the application belongs to the intended organization before interpreting cross-org acceptance as a bug. Wrong organization ownership can make a token legitimately valid for that app.
oidc_jwt.source: Core concepts; Shared application docs; Public API M2M guidance

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC/OAuth callback tests involving localhost desktop clients, redirect_uri matching is exact except where the application explicitly allows wildcard localhost patterns such as http://127.0.0.1:*/callback or http://localhost:*/callback. Do not generalize wildcard acceptance to normal web apps; use exact redirect URIs unless the application configuration explicitly documents wildcard localhost callbacks.
oidc_jwt.source: MCP connect docs; Dynamic client registration docs; Application config docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Casdoor supports Dynamic Client Registration at /api/oauth/register, advertised via /.well-known/openid-configuration registration_endpoint. DCR requires at least one redirect_uris entry. If DCR is disabled by organization policy, registration failure is by design and must not be treated as an auth-flow bug.

For authorization code flows that use RFC 8707 resource indicators, the resource parameter MUST match exactly between /login/oauth/authorize and /api/login/oauth/access_token. If they differ, audience-binding tests are invalid because Casdoor documents exact matching between authorization and token requests.

For PKCE tests, when code_challenge/code_challenge_method=S256 are sent to /login/oauth/authorize, the token request to /api/login/oauth/access_token MUST include the original code_verifier. Casdoor documents PKCE support and says client_secret becomes optional only when PKCE is enabled; if client_secret is provided, it must still be correct.

For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch and flow-coherence tests, include redirect_uri in the token request only if the client flow actually used it and ensure it exactly matches the registered redirect URI and the authorization request value. Casdoor documentation repeatedly requires exact callback/redirect URL matching across provider, Casdoor application, and client flow.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against access tokens, include a CONTROL login using a valid token acquisition flow first. A failed token use without a control may reflect broken client/application setup rather than token freshness enforcement.

Cookie/session lifetime has a numeric sentinel: CookieExpireInHours value 0 means use the default lifetime, not immediate expiry. Documentation also states that without Remember me, session is limited to 24h. Do not use 0 in freshness tests expecting instant expiration.

Casdoor access_token and id_token are documented as the same JWT payload and can be used interchangeably. Do NOT flag identical claims across access_token and id_token as over-issuance by itself; this is by design. However, session_token for API calls must still use access_token in the harness.

For I5 audience-binding tests, when resource is supplied during authorization/token exchange, the resulting access token aud becomes the resource URI instead of the client_id. Test oracles must compare aud against the requested resource in that case, not against client_id.

For cross-organization and shared-application tests, shared applications intentionally use organization-qualified identifiers by appending -org-<organizationName> to client_id or application name. Do not treat acceptance of org-suffixed client IDs as cross-tenant confusion; this is the documented addressing scheme for shared applications.

For multi-tenant setup, owner semantics differ by resource type in documentation: applications are owned by the creating organization/admin context, while users belong to exactly one organization and are identified as <organization>/<username>. Fuzzers must preserve organization-qualified user identifiers in permission and identity tests to avoid false cross-user collisions.

Casdoor can automatically link OAuth logins to existing users by OAuth identity, email/phone, or username (case-insensitive). For I4 collision tests involving upstream OAuth/OIDC identities, disable or account for automatic account linking; otherwise two upstream identities may merge by design rather than due to a broker flaw.

For I4 case-confusion tests, documentation states automatic account linking can use username case-insensitively and Casdoor also has an isUsernameLowered option. Do not treat case-folded merges as unexpected unless the test explicitly controls these settings.

For I4 username-mapping tests on SAML/OAuth upstreams, some providers intentionally derive the Casdoor username from provider-specific fields with fallback logic (for example Lark prefers UserId then UnionId then OpenId; SAML falls back to email then NameID when username mapping is absent). The oracle must compare against the documented derived identifier, not the raw upstream display field.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on token exchange, request a narrowed scope subset and verify the exchanged token does not exceed the subject token scope. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the original scope, while provided scope should be a subset for downscoping. A test that omits scope cannot claim escalation if the new token matches the original scope.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests against MCP or API consumers, session/cookie authentication bypasses scope checking and grants full tool access by design. Use Bearer access tokens, not browser session cookies, when testing scope enforcement.

For I1/I5 audience tests involving MCP or resource indicators, the aud claim must match the exact resource URI including scheme, host, and port. Documentation explicitly warns that mismatched resource/audience values cause unauthorized results. Use exact URI equality, not prefix or wildcard matching, in test setup.

For DCR-based tests, redirect_uris are required and must match exactly character-for-character during OAuth. DCR failures such as invalid_redirect_uri or invalid_client_metadata are setup errors, not security findings.

Applications created through Dynamic Client Registration are tagged with dcr and receive default settings including 7-day token expiration. Do not compare DCR-created clients against manually created clients without normalizing these defaults, or freshness/authorization results may differ by configuration rather than vulnerability.

Exclusive sign-in invalidates prior sessions for the same user and application on each new login. In multi-login sequences, a second successful login can legitimately revoke the first token/session. Do not flag subsequent failure of the first session as replay protection or flow breakage; it is configured behavior.

Casdoor's token endpoint expects JSON request bodies in the documentation examples for authorization_code, password, client_credentials, refresh_token, and token-exchange grants. Do not send form-encoded bodies to /api/login/oauth/access_token unless you have separately confirmed support; use JSON for these grant flows.

For RFC 8707 resource indicator tests, if start_oidc_auth includes resource, exchange_code_for_token MUST include the exact same resource value. Casdoor documents exact matching between authorization and token requests; mismatches will fail for configuration reasons rather than revealing an audience-binding bug.

For I5 audience-binding tests on authorization-code flow, use the resource parameter because Casdoor sets the access token aud claim to the resource URI instead of the client_id when resource is supplied. Do not expect aud=client_id in those cases.

For I2 freshness tests, application ExpireInHours and RefreshExpireInHours are in hours, while token endpoint responses return expires_in as a numeric value shown in examples. Build attack/control tokens relative to {{now_epoch}} and configure application lifetimes carefully; do not assume per-second admin configuration knobs from the response field alone.

Numeric sentinel: application CodeResendTimeout uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'use the global default', not literal zero seconds. Never assume 0 disables waiting; set an explicit positive value when testing resend timing behavior.

Numeric sentinel: refresh token expiration default is 0 hours at the application level. Documentation states you must set Refresh Token expiration on the application to use refresh tokens. Treat 0 as effectively disabled/not usable for refresh testing, not as infinite lifetime.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, always run a control login with a valid token or valid authorization flow in the same application first. A failed attack login can also be caused by disabled grant types, missing redirect URI, missing provider attachment, or application tag restrictions.

For I3 config-change tests involving application settings, new logins after an admin changes RedirectUris, GrantTypes, TokenFormat, scopes, or provider attachments are expected to follow the new configuration immediately. Do not flag success under the new config as a coherence bug; only flag stale acceptance under the old config when the old behavior should no longer be valid.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on token_exchange, request a narrower baseline scope first, then attempt exchange with a broader scope. Casdoor documents that omitted scope inherits the subject token scope, while provided scope is intended for narrowing. Any broader result must be compared against the original granted scope, not against application defaults.

For token_exchange audience tests, Casdoor's token exchange endpoint is the same /api/login/oauth/access_token endpoint and uses subject_token_type values urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token, urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt, or urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token. Use the documented token type explicitly to avoid false negatives from parser rejection.

For OIDC callback tests with PKCE, when code_challenge/code_challenge_method were sent at authorization time, exchange_code_for_token should include code_verifier. Casdoor documents PKCE support and states client_secret becomes optional only when PKCE is enabled; missing code_verifier may fail for normal PKCE enforcement rather than indicating another bug.

For OIDC SSO audience-cross-tenant style tests, each application has its own RedirectUris and client credentials. Ensure the authorization request and token exchange use the same application's client_id and redirect_uri. Cross-application reuse of a code can fail due to redirect/client mismatch rather than aud validation.

Casdoor applications can be shared across organizations by appending -org-<organizationName> to the client_id or application name. For multi-tenant I4/I5 tests, treat org-suffixed shared-app client IDs as distinct relying-party identifiers; do not collapse them with the base client_id when evaluating cross-org acceptance.

Application tags restrict sign-in: only users with at least one matching tag may access the application, except admins/global admins. For identity-binding tests, ensure both test users satisfy the same application tag policy or use untagged applications; otherwise login failures are expected policy outcomes.

Organization setting isUsernameLowered can lowercase usernames. For I4 case-confusion tests, check whether the target organization lowers usernames before treating Admin vs admin convergence as a vulnerability.

Organization setting 'Use email as username' causes email to become the username when username is hidden at signup, and username updates when email changes. For I4 tests comparing sent identity to granted identity, avoid signup flows that derive username from email unless that derivation is the intended oracle.

Casdoor's /api/userinfo returns claims according to granted scope and token format. Missing email/profile/phone/address fields are not authorization bugs if the corresponding scopes were not requested or the token format omits them. Compare only claims implied by the requested scope and configured token format.

For address-claim tests, only JWT-Standard yields an OIDC-compliant address object in tokens. Other token formats return address as a raw string array or /api/userinfo may return Location as a plain string for address scope. Do not flag this as type confusion unless the application was explicitly configured for JWT-Standard and still violates the documented format.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: A pre-configured test environment exists: organization 'test-org', application 'app-test' (query clientId/clientSecret via GET /api/get-application?id=admin/app-test), and SAML provider 'provider-saml-test' already linked to app-test. For MOST tests, REUSE these resources instead of creating new ones. Only create new organizations/applications when the attack specifically requires distinct tenants (e.g., I5 cross-org token exchange). OWNERSHIP RULES: Applications and providers MUST use owner='admin'. Users MUST use owner=<organization_name> (e.g., 'test-org'). NEVER use 'built-in' as organization for create_user — the built-in org forbids user creation. GRANT TYPES: When creating applications, ALWAYS include grantTypes=['password','authorization_code','urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange'] and enablePassword=true and cert='cert-built-in' unless the test specifically requires otherwise. MULTI-APP SEQUENCES: When a test needs two separate applications (e.g., token exchange between different clients/audiences), use 'app-test' as the SOURCE application (already exists) and create ONE new application as the TARGET. Create users with signupApplication matching the app they will login to. For login_with_password, the executor auto-resolves client_id from the user's signupApplication — so set signupApplication correctly in create_user.
